cvEn:
Natan Saban, son of Revital and Ilan, was born on the 25th of Elul 5761 (13 September 2001) in Bat Yam. Natan, "Nat'on" to those who loved him, was very attached to his family.

Natan was a sensitive and quiet child with a winning smile. He had a big heart, always considered others, and worked to create a good atmosphere. Above all, he held to the value of giving. He was always the first to volunteer for any task, without asking for anything in return.

As a child he attended kindergartens in Bat Yam, where he grew up, and later went to a Chabad school in Rishon LeZion. After finishing elementary school, he studied at the "Zion-Blumental" boarding school in Jerusalem, and afterwards at the "Amit HaOfek" educational institution in Or Akiva, class of 16.

Natan was very well liked by his friends and teachers. He was endowed with great curiosity and showed keen interest in his studies. He did not shy away from challenges, set himself goals and worked to achieve them. Over the years he received certificates of excellence for his academic achievements, and in twelfth grade he was chosen as the Amit Network's outstanding student for 2019, for his contribution to the community and his academic excellence.

In his free time he liked to spend time with friends, ride the motorcycle he had bought, or lie on the sofa in the living room and watch television.

On 11 August 2020 he enlisted in the IDF and served in the Givati Brigade.

During his training course, on 9 October 2020, Natan was killed in a road accident while riding his motorcycle.

Private Natan Saban fell during his service on the 21st of Tishrei 5781 (9 October 2020). He was nineteen years old when he fell. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Holon. He is survived by his parents and siblings.

After his death he was promoted to Corporal.

His loved ones wrote on his headstone: "Natan, you are our gift. Your memory will never leave our hearts forever."

His girlfriend Chen wrote: "You were such a good person with a giant heart, a great soul. When people looked into your eyes they saw how much you wanted to give, how strong you were, how much love there was in you. You could not be ignored. You left so many memories that you cannot even process that you are gone. I so hope that it is good for you now up there, and I will always miss you and will never really accept that you are not here."

On the thirtieth day after Natan's fall, a ceremony in his memory was held at Amit HaOfek High School, at which a book produced to commemorate him was launched. At the memorial gathering his teacher Rachel wrote: "Natan, my beloved and dear student, another year in which we remember and grieve your needless loss. A student loved by all, the first to volunteer for every task, willingly and without asking for anything in return. As your name, so were you, a heart full of giving. May your memory be blessed and kept in our hearts forever."

Natan is commemorated on the Gilad website, established in memory of all the fallen of the Givati Brigade.
